name: Semantic Recommendation Relevance
evaluation_unit: one user query x one recommended book
purpose: Judge how well a recommended book's supplied description satisfies the semantic intent of the user's natural-language request.
evidence_rules: Use the supplied book description as the primary evidence.
The title and author may provide supporting context, but must not override the description.
Do not use external knowledge about the book when the supplied description does not establish a claim.
Judge semantic relevance only. Ignore category-filter correctness, recommendation count, retrieval rank, and tone-ordering behavior.
Do not reward isolated keyword overlap when the central intent is not satisfied.
tie_break_rule: If a case genuinely falls between two adjacent scores, assign the lower score unless the higher score is clearly supported.

4.label: Strong
4.definition: The book directly and strongly matches the central semantic intent of the request; a reasonable reader would regard it as an obvious or direct recommendation.

3.label: Good / Clear
3.definition: The book is clearly relevant overall, but one important aspect of the request is secondary, implicit, weaker, or missing.

2.label: Partial
2.definition: The book meaningfully satisfies one central part of the request but misses another central part; there is substantive semantic overlap.

1.label: Weak / Incidental
1.definition: There is a genuine requested concept or close equivalent, but it is peripheral or incidental; the book is not really about the request.

0.label: None
0.definition: The supplied evidence does not establish meaningful relevance to the request, or meaningfully contradicts it; speculation is not evidence.

boundary_guidance: When between adjacent scores, choose the lower score unless the higher score is clearly supported.
A directly mentioned concept can still be incidental if it functions only as background, an example, or a passing detail.
A missing central component normally prevents a strong score even when other components match well.
